name: Hack Squat
summary: A machine squat performed on an angled sled with the back supported. It allows deep, stable quad-focused squatting with little demand on balance.
setup: Step into the machine and place your shoulders under the pads with your back flat against the pad.
Set your feet about shoulder width apart, a little forward on the platform, with toes turned out slightly.
Hold the handles and release the safety stops.
Stand up to the start position without locking your knees hard.
execution: Brace your trunk and lower under control by bending your knees and hips.
Keep your whole foot on the platform and your knees tracking over your toes.
Descend until your thighs are at least parallel, or as deep as you can while keeping your back and hips on the pad.
Drive through the whole foot to return to the top, stopping just short of lockout.
Re-engage the safety stops when finished.
mistakes: Heels lifting off the platform: move your feet slightly forward or higher on the plate.
Hips tucking under at the bottom as the lower back rounds: shorten the depth to where the pelvis stays on the pad.
Knees drifting inward: push them out in line with the toes and use a lighter load.
Bouncing at the bottom: pause briefly and drive up smoothly.
